techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment included in the Windows operating system. PowerShell can also be installed on Linux and macOS. Adversaries can use PowerShell to perform a number of actions, including discovery of information and execution of code. Examples include the Start-Process cmdlet which can be used to run an executable and the Invoke-Command cmdlet which runs a command locally or on a remote computer (though administrator permissions are required to use PowerShell to connect to remote systems). PowerShell may also be used to download and run executables from the Internet, which can be executed from disk or in memory without touching disk. A number of PowerShell-based offensive testing tools are available, including Empire, PowerSploit, PoshC2, and PSAttack.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Privileged Account Management focuses on implementing policies, controls, and tools to securely manage privileged accounts (e.g., SYSTEM, root, or administrative accounts).

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Prevent the execution of unauthorized or malicious code on systems by implementing application control, script blocking, and other execution prevention mechanisms. This ensures that only trusted and authorized code is executed, reducing the risk of malware and unauthorized actions.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Disable or remove unnecessary and potentially vulnerable software, features, or services to reduce the attack surface and prevent abuse by adversaries. This involves identifying software or features that are no longer needed or that could be exploited and ensuring they are either removed or properly disabled.

mitigations.name: Code Signing
mitigations.description: Code Signing is a security process that ensures the authenticity and integrity of software by digitally signing executables, scripts, and other code artifacts. It prevents untrusted or malicious code from executing by verifying the digital signatures against trusted sources.

mitigations.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
mitigations.description: Antivirus/Antimalware solutions utilize signatures, heuristics, and behavioral analysis to detect, block, and remediate malicious software, including viruses, trojans, ransomware, and spyware. These solutions continuously monitor endpoints and systems for known malicious patterns and suspicious behaviors that indicate compromise.

detections.name: Abuse of PowerShell for Arbitrary Execution

analytics.description: Detects behavioral chains where PowerShell is launched with encoded commands, unusual parent processes, or suspicious modules loaded, potentially followed by network connections or child process spawning. Supports detection of both direct (powershell.exe) and indirect (.NET automation) invocations.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment. Tools or files may be copied from an external adversary-controlled system to the victim network through the command and control channel or through alternate protocols such as ftp. Once present, adversaries may also transfer/spread tools between victim devices within a compromised environment (i.e. Lateral Tool Transfer). On Windows, adversaries may use various utilities to download tools, such as `copy`, `finger`, certutil, and PowerShell commands such as IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).downloadString() and Invoke-WebRequest. On Linux and macOS systems, a variety of utilities also exist, such as `curl`, `scp`, `sftp`, `tftp`, `rsync`, `finger`, and `wget`. A number of these tools, such as `wget`, `curl`, and `scp`, also exist on ESXi.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.description: Use intrusion detection signatures to block traffic at network boundaries.

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.description: Employ network appliances and endpoint software to filter ingress, egress, and lateral network traffic. This includes protocol-based filtering, enforcing firewall rules, and blocking or restricting traffic based on predefined conditions to limit adversary movement and data exfiltration.

detections.name: Detect Ingress Tool Transfers via Behavioral Chain

analytics.description: Unusual or uncommon processes initiate network connections to external destinations followed by file creation (tools downloaded).
Shell-based tools (curl, wget, scp) initiate connections to external domains followed by creation of executable files on disk.
Process execution of curl or wget followed by a network connection and a file created in temporary or user-specific directories.
Command line interface or vCLI triggers remote transfer using wget or curl, writing files into datastore paths or local tmp directories.

playbook.title: Response Playbook for PowerShell-based Ingress Tool Transfer on SALES-PC-11
playbook.executive_summary: A hidden PowerShell process launched from Word on SALES-PC-11 downloaded and executed a remote script from a suspicious IP, indicating a high‑severity compromise. Immediate containment, evidence preservation, and eradication are required, followed by system recovery and hardening to prevent recurrence.

detection_and_analysis.action: Collect volatile memory and process state from SALES-PC-11
detection_and_analysis.detail: Use a trusted forensic tool to acquire a RAM image and list of running processes, preserving the PowerShell command line and parent-child relationship.

detection_and_analysis.action: Query Sysmon and PowerShell event logs for related activity
detection_and_analysis.detail: Search WinEventLog:Sysmon and WinEventLog:PowerShell for EventID 1/ProcessCreate with parent WINWORD.EXE and EventID 4104 with encoded commands, correlating timestamps with the download request.
Review firewall and NetFlow logs for outbound HTTP(S) traffic from SALES-PC-11 at the time of the PowerShell execution.

containment.action: Isolate SALES-PC-11 from the corporate network
containment.detail: Place the host in a quarantine VLAN or disable its network port to stop further C2 or lateral movement.
Use taskkill or remote management to stop the specific powershell.exe instance identified by its PID.

containment.action: Block the malicious IP address at the perimeter
containment.detail: Add 185.220.101.4 to the deny list on the firewall and enable outbound filtering for HTTP downloads.

eradication.detail: Remove the file and any other artifacts created in the TEMP directory, verifying no residual scheduled tasks remain.

eradication.action: Run an endpoint antivirus/antimalware scan with full heuristics
eradication.detail: Trigger M1049 scanning on the host to detect any additional payloads or persistence mechanisms.

eradication.action: Revoke and reset credentials for CORP\m.ali
eradication.detail: Force password change and invalidate any active tokens to eliminate potential credential abuse.

recovery.action: Restore system files from a known-good baseline
recovery.detail: Use D3-RF to replace any modified binaries (e.g., PowerShell modules) with clean copies from the baseline image.
Return the host to production once scans are clean and logs show no further malicious activity.

hardening.action: Enable PowerShell script block logging and constrained language mode
hardening.detail: Configure Group Policy to enforce detailed logging and restrict script capabilities to approved scripts only.

hardening.action: Apply executable allowlisting for PowerShell and Office binaries
hardening.detail: Deploy D3-EAL to allow only signed Microsoft binaries, blocking unknown PowerShell invocations from Office processes.

hardening.action: Implement outbound web filtering for unknown domains
hardening.detail: Configure D3-NTF to require proxy inspection for HTTP downloads and block direct connections to untrusted IPs.

hunt_leads.look_for: ProcessCreate events where parent image is WINWORD.EXE and child image is powershell.exe with hidden window flags
Script block logging entries containing Invoke-WebRequest to external IPs
Outbound HTTP GET to 185.220.101.4 or other low‑reputation IPs from internal workstations
